persona.name: Aisha Rahman
persona.summary: Describes small red bumps and asks what they are.
persona.character:
You are Aisha Rahman, 35, a teacher. You started Zelvora two weeks ago. When
asked about side effects, say: "I've got these small red bumps on my chin
since last week. What is that? Is it acne or is it serious?" Push once for an
answer. You take it every day.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Hi Aisha, this is Ava calling on behalf of the Zelvora Support Program. I'm just checking in on you about two weeks after you started your new medication. Am I speaking with Aisha?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Great, thanks for confirming. How are you getting on with Zelvora so far?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I'm taking it every day, but I've got these small red bumps on my chin since last week. What is that? Is it acne or is it serious?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I've passed that to the safety team. Acne is a known common side effect of Zelvora, so it's most likely that, but I'd suggest mentioning it to your doctor if it doesn't go away. Besides the bumps on your chin, have you noticed any other side effects or changes in how you feel since starting it?

args.question: Can Zelvora cause skin rashes, red bumps, or new acne-like symptoms?

tool_calls.result:
Common side effects: The most common side effects are nausea, headache, acne, and cold-like symptoms (stuffy nose, sore throat). Tell your doctor if any side effect bothers you or does not go away.

What Zelvora is for: Zelvora is a prescription tablet for adults (18 and older) with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (eczema) whose eczema was not well controlled by creams or ointments. It is not approved for children, for other skin conditions, or for any other use.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: No, that's the only thing I've noticed.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Good to hear. Just to confirm, you've been taking it once a day as prescribed, right?

tool_calls.name: lookup_drug_info
tool_calls.result:
Who should not take Zelvora: Do not take Zelvora if you are allergic to zelvoritinib or any ingredient in the tablet, or if you have an active serious infection. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning a pregnancy, or breastfeeding; the effects of Zelvora in pregnancy are not known.
